refusals.consequence: Flood is UNKNOWN for every parcel, with reason `nfhl_robots_disallow`. It is not "no flood risk" and it is not a zero penalty — a parcel we are not allowed to check is exactly as unmeasured as one outside NFHL coverage. pipeline/enrich/nfhl.ts implements the derivation and is unit-tested against fixtures, but NOTHING CALLS IT OVER THE NETWORK and the orchestrator refuses to. Re-check this file if FEMA's robots.txt changes; flipping the lane back on is a registry edit, not a code change.

Road access is UNKNOWN for every parcel, with reason `tiger_robots_unobtainable`, which is the branch plan §5.6 pre-authorised ("if it fails, road access renders `unknown` permanently"). Two things would have gone wrong had this been treated as a normal robots.txt: robots-parser finds zero directives in HTML and returns ALLOWED, and the rotating support ID would move the source to ingest_paused on every single run. guard.ts looksLikeRobotsTxt() now refuses a non-empty body carrying no recognisable directive, so the false permit is closed for every host, not just this one.
